draft.title: Substitution and addition reactions
card: Substitution
A saturated alkane has only single C-C bonds. In a substitution reaction, a halogen atom replaces a hydrogen atom on the alkane. A hydrogen halide is also made.
Conditions
Alkanes react with chlorine or bromine only when UV light is present. For example, CH4 + Cl2 gives CH3Cl + HCl. The products are a haloalkane and a hydrogen halide.
Addition
An unsaturated alkene has a C=C double bond. In an addition reaction, one bond of the double bond opens and a new atom bonds to each carbon. Only one product is made.
Reagents
Alkenes add H2 to give an alkane, Cl2 or Br2 to give a dihaloalkane, HCl or HBr to give a haloalkane, and H2O to give an alcohol.
draft.remember: Alkanes substitute and make two products. Alkenes add and make one product.

a.q: Which description fits the reaction of ethene with bromine to make 1,2-dibromoethane?
opts: Addition, because the C=C bond opens and one product forms
Substitution, because bromine replaces hydrogen atoms
Addition, because HBr forms as a second product
Substitution, because the C=C bond opens and gives one product
a.why: Ethene has a C=C double bond. One bond opens and a bromine atom joins each carbon, giving a single product, which is addition. Substitution would replace hydrogen and also make a hydrogen halide.
a.clue: Count the products and check what happens to the double bond.

b.q: Ethane reacts with chlorine in UV light. Ethene reacts with chlorine in the same flask. Which statement is correct?
opts: Ethane gives chloroethane and HCl; ethene gives C2H4Cl2
Ethane gives C2H4Cl2; ethene gives chloroethane and HCl
Both give chloroethane and HCl as the two products
Both give a dichloro product as the only product
b.why: Ethane is saturated, so chlorine substitutes for a hydrogen and HCl forms. Ethene is unsaturated, so chlorine adds across the C=C bond to give one product, 1,2-dichloroethane (C2H4Cl2). The reverse option swaps the two reaction types.
b.clue: Ask which molecule has a double bond and which reaction gives two products.

problems.detail: "Alkanes react with chlorine or bromine only when UV light is present" is too absolute. Alkane halogenation can also be started by high temperature. Better: "need UV light (or heat) to react".

"Only one product is made" in addition is not always true. HCl, HBr or H2O adding to an unsymmetrical alkene such as propene can give two isomeric products. Better: "one product (for a symmetrical alkene such as ethene)" or "can make one product".

"Alkanes substitute and make two products" oversimplifies. Further substitution can give a mixture of haloalkanes. A softer wording, such as "a haloalkane and a hydrogen halide", would avoid teaching an absolute rule.
"Ethene reacts with chlorine in the same flask" is confusing. It suggests both hydrocarbons are mixed together and competing for chlorine. "Separately, under the same conditions" would be clearer.

check.summary: Both questions have one clear right answer, and the explanations agree with it. The card overstates two rules: halogenation can be started by heat as well as UV light, and addition to an unsymmetrical alkene can give two products. The phrase "in the same flask" in question b is ambiguous.
